podcast.title: Interest in Jamie Hewlett's Work
podcast.body: Before the 1995 "Tank Girl" movie, Steven Spielberg was interested in working with Jamie Hewlett, indicating Hewlett's early prominence as a comic book artist. "But actually before that happened, Steven Spielberg was interested in working with Jamie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Kubrick's "AI" Film Project and Jourgensen's Antics
xref.body: Al Jourgensen was reportedly approached by director Stanley Kubrick to compose music for a new film titled "AI." Despite Kubrick's admiration for Ministry, Jourgensen repeatedly insisted that "AI" actually stood for "anal intruder" and suggested the project should instead be a porn film. Following Kubrick's death, Steven Spielberg had to intervene to "clean things up" and resolve the situation caused by Jourgensen's disruptive behavior regarding the film. "He somehow got mixed up with director Stanley Kubrick, who wanted him to write music for a new film. He was going to call AI."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Real Estate Career - Selling to Celebrities
xref.body: In the 1980s, Linda shifted careers to become a real estate agent and was highly successful, selling properties to notable figures like Sting, Angelina Jolie, and Steven Spielberg. She was also reportedly the inspiration for the real estate agent character in Oliver Stone's movie "Wall Street." "But in the 1980s, she decided that she had had enough and became a real estate agent. She did very, very well selling houses and apartments and condos to people like Sting, an Angelina Jolie and Steven Spielberg."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Tank Girl Movie
xref.body: His comic strip "Tank Girl" was optioned for a movie, which was made in 1995. Prior to this, Steven Spielberg had expressed interest in working with Hewlett. "It was option for a movie that was made in 1995."
